key_insight: Effective code-interpreter reasoning is associated with more crucial tokens and more code-specific cognitive behaviors, especially verification, backtracking, and backward chaining.
engineering_relevance: These properties can be injected at inference or training time to improve some reasoning tasks and make CI-based LLM reasoning more token-efficient.
method: Compare extrinsic properties (crucial tokens) vs. intrinsic properties (cognitive behaviors) across multiple LLMs.
Use crucial-token appending at inference and behavior augmentation during supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.
Analyze effects on reasoning quality, overthinking, and token efficiency across models and tasks.
evidence_signal: The authors evaluate multiple LLMs and report gains on mathematical, ordering, and optimization reasoning, with training improvements in two of three evaluated models.
watch_item: Benefits are task- and model-dependent, so added tokens or behavioral augmentation may not generalize uniformly and can yield limited gains in some models.
paper_title: Exploring Extrinsic and Intrinsic Properties for Effective Reasoning with Code Interpreter
